answer: Canyon clock: each identity runs its own sequential VDF chain, so every fake costs one dedicated CPU core full-time (~$5/month; 1,000 fakes = 1,000 cores). The chain is seeded by the identity's key and the epoch beacon, so it can't be shared or copied between names. At a random moment the ledger names a trellis of 12 checkpoints; the agent must reveal them with Wesolowski proofs verifiers check in milliseconds, and a gap or mismatch is a sable mark that voids that epoch's pay. Sequential squaring can't be parallelized, so bulk hardware buys no speedup; a rich farm still pays linearly.
